title: Slack: antenna tilt drifts after storms
description: A radio specialist explains a site-specific quirk on Slack. Tests the slack channel and a narrow binding to the instance RAD-221 and its site; swapping the unit is the thing to avoid.
subject: #field-north

incident.summary: Low throughput on RAD-221 after last night's storm

messages.text: RAD-221 on Kemijärvi hill has had poor throughput since last night's storm. I'm planning to swap the unit tomorrow and will bring a spare RU-200.
Remember the barrier key from the service station!
Hold on before you swap it. After storms the antenna tilt on RAD-221 drifts, that mast is very exposed. Check the antenna alignment first. I have fixed it three times with a ten minute re-tilt.
So the unit itself is fine? Why do you think so?
The RU-200 has been solid. It's the mount that moves in strong wind. A new unit would drift too.
Re-aligned the antenna. Throughput is back to normal 🎉
Good. Note it down: check the tilt after every storm.

items.summary: After storms the antenna tilt on RAD-221 drifts; check and correct the alignment before replacing the radio unit.
items.diagnosis: antenna mount drifts in strong wind, the radio unit is fine
items.action: Check the antenna alignment and re-tilt it before replacing the radio unit.
items.evidence: seq 7: 'Re-aligned the antenna. Throughput is back to normal'
